guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.title: HEIC to JPG: Convert iPhone Wedding Photos Safely
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.desc: Why iPhone wedding photos arrive as HEIC, how to convert them to JPG for labs and guests, and what to check so dates and quality survive.
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.lead: HEIC is a smaller, newer container that many print labs, older computers and upload forms still reject. Convert copies, not your only originals.
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.f1v: Apple's HEIC/HEIF image container, common on iPhones
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.f2v: JPG works with labs, Windows, most browsers and older devices
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.f3v: Export at 90–95% JPEG to avoid a visible second compression
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.f4v: Preserve the HEIC originals and their capture dates
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.s1: Convert in one batch, exporting to a separate folder so the originals stay untouched. Check that the converted files keep the capture date — some converters reset it to the conversion time, which destroys the chronological order you need for an album. If the photos were shot in HDR or with Live Photo enabled, decide whether you want the still frame or the motion version before converting.
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.s2: iPhones default to 'High Efficiency' (HEIC) in many regions, while Android devices more often produce JPEG or a vendor Raw format. Printing labs in the US and Europe overwhelmingly request JPEG or TIFF; some online portals now accept HEIC but their colour handling varies. If you are collecting photos from guests across both platforms, ask for JPEG up front to avoid a mixed set.
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.s3: Do not convert by taking a screenshot, and do not use a converter that silently downsizes the image. Watch for a colour shift on wide-gamut (P3) photos, which can look flat after conversion to sRGB. Also confirm that orientation metadata carried over — a rotated portrait is the most common conversion surprise.
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.q1: Why are my iPhone photos HEIC?
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.a1: iPhones use High Efficiency capture by default to save storage. You can switch the camera to 'Most Compatible' to record JPEG instead.
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.q2: Does converting to JPG lose quality?
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.a2: A small amount, since JPEG is lossy. Export at 90–95% once from the original and avoid repeated saves.
guides.heic-to-jpg-wedding-photos.a3: Some labs accept them, but JPEG or TIFF is far more reliable. Check the lab's file requirements before ordering.
